use: Rejects an expectation and goes further the other way: 'far from cheap, it cost double'.
name: far from
formation: noun or plain form + dokoro ka

example.romaji: yasumu dokoro ka, kyuujitsu mo shigoto da yo
example.ja: 休むどころか、休日も仕事だよ
example.english: Rest? I'm even working my days off.

examplePolite.romaji: yasumu dokoro ka, kyuujitsu mo shigoto desu yo
examplePolite.ja: 休むどころか、休日も仕事ですよ
examplePolite.english: Far from resting, I'm working even on my days off.

notes: 'sore dokoro ja nai' = there's no time for that right now. Compare dake de naku, a neutral 'not only'.

use: The second half usually has mo: 'not only X, Y too'.
name: not only
formation: noun or plain form + dake de naku

example.romaji: ano mise, oishii dake ja nakute yasui n da yo
example.ja: あの店、おいしいだけじゃなくて安いんだよ
example.english: That place isn't just tasty, it's cheap too.

examplePolite.romaji: ano mise wa oishii dake de naku, yasui n desu yo
examplePolite.ja: あの店はおいしいだけでなく、安いんですよ
examplePolite.english: That restaurant is not only good but cheap as well.

notes: Speech usually says dake ja nakute; dake de naku sounds formal or written.

english: rather than; or rather; more like
use: Corrects your own word choice: 'not so much X as Y'.
name: rather than
formation: noun or plain form + to iu yori

example.romaji: samui to iu yori, mou itai yo
example.ja: 寒いというより、もう痛いよ
example.english: It's not so much cold as painful.

examplePolite.romaji: samui to iu yori, mou itai desu ne
examplePolite.ja: 寒いというより、もう痛いですね
examplePolite.english: It's less cold than actually painful.

notes: Casual: 'tte iu yori'. The stand-alone filler 'to iu ka' (or rather) is even more common.

use: Picks an extreme case to make the point: 'even the teacher couldn't'.
name: even
formation: noun + de sae; after another particle, plain sae

example.romaji: sensei de sae wakaranakatta n da yo
example.ja: 先生でさえわからなかったんだよ

examplePolite.ja: 先生でさえわかりませんでした
examplePolite.english: Even the teacher couldn't work it out.

notes: Casual talk usually says de mo or sura: 'kodomo de mo wakaru'. Don't mix with sae ... -ba, 'as long as'.

english: as (a role); in the capacity of
use: Names the role, status or purpose: 'as a teacher', 'as a present'.
name: as (a role)

example.romaji: tomodachi to shite suki na dake da yo
example.ja: 友達として好きなだけだよ
example.english: I just like him as a friend.

examplePolite.romaji: tomodachi to shite suki na dake desu
examplePolite.ja: 友達として好きなだけです
examplePolite.english: I only like him as a friend.

notes: 'watashi to shite wa' = speaking for myself. Not the -te form of -ou to suru (try to).

english: for; to (from someone's point of view)
use: Says who something matters to or how it looks to them, not who benefits.
name: for (someone)

example.romaji: watashi ni totte, kazoku ga ichiban daiji
example.ja: 私にとって、家族が一番大事

examplePolite.romaji: watashi ni totte, kazoku ga ichiban daiji desu
examplePolite.ja: 私にとって、家族が一番大事です
examplePolite.english: To me, family is the most important thing.

notes: For 'for your benefit' use no tame ni; for a gift just ni: 'kore, anata ni'.

use: Marks who an attitude or action is aimed at: 'rude to customers', 'angry at him'.
name: toward
formation: noun + ni taishite; before a noun: ni taisuru

example.romaji: kare, okyakusan ni taishite taido warui yo ne
example.ja: 彼、お客さんに対して態度悪いよね
example.english: He's got a bad attitude toward customers, hasn't he?

examplePolite.romaji: kare wa okyakusan ni taishite taido ga warui desu ne
examplePolite.ja: 彼はお客さんに対して態度が悪いですね
examplePolite.english: He's quite rude to customers, isn't he?

notes: Second use is contrast, 'whereas': 'ani ni taishite, otouto wa ...' (unlike his older brother, ...).

use: The formal ni tsuite, for meetings, emails and announcements.
name: concerning
formation: noun + ni kanshite; before a noun: ni kansuru

example.romaji: sono ken ni kanshite wa, ato de gorenraku shimasu
example.ja: その件に関しては、後でご連絡します
example.english: I'll get back to you about that later.

notes: In casual talk say ni tsuite instead. Before nouns: 'kankyou ni kansuru nyuusu' (news about the environment).

use: Says who a product or service is designed for: 'for kids', 'for beginners'.
name: made for
formation: noun + muke (no + noun); noun + muke ni

example.romaji: kono anime, kodomo muke ja nai yo
example.ja: このアニメ、子供向けじゃないよ

examplePolite.romaji: kono anime wa kodomo muke ja arimasen yo
examplePolite.ja: このアニメは子供向けじゃありませんよ
examplePolite.english: This anime isn't meant for children.

notes: Don't mix with -muki, 'suited to': shoshinsha muki means it happens to suit beginners, muke that it was made for them.

use: Labels a person, look or thing by its type: 'oshare kei' (the stylish type).
name: -type

example.romaji: karai kei no tabemono, daisuki nan da
example.ja: 辛い系の食べ物、大好きなんだ

examplePolite.romaji: karai kei no tabemono ga daisuki nan desu
examplePolite.ja: 辛い系の食べ物が大好きなんです
examplePolite.english: I really love spicy kinds of food.

notes: Standard, not slang, in rikei and bunkei (science and arts tracks). Like 'tte kanji', it keeps a label vague.

use: Noun + goto keeps the whole thing together ('skin and all'); -goto ni means each or every.
name: and all / every
formation: noun + goto; noun or counter + goto ni

example.romaji: kono budou, kawa goto taberareru yo
example.ja: このぶどう、皮ごと食べられるよ
example.english: You can eat these grapes skin and all.

examplePolite.romaji: kono budou wa kawa goto taberaremasu yo
examplePolite.ja: このぶどうは皮ごと食べられますよ
examplePolite.english: You can eat these grapes with the skin on.

notes: With ni it means 'every': 'ichi jikan goto ni' (every hour). 'marugoto' = whole, entirely.

use: Doing something without a thing; also nashi ni and, in speech, nashi ja.
name: without

example.romaji: koohii nashi ja ikite ikenai yo
example.ja: コーヒーなしじゃ生きていけないよ

examplePolite.romaji: koohii nashi de wa ikite ikemasen
examplePolite.ja: コーヒーなしでは生きていけません

notes: When ordering, 'X nashi de' = hold the X: 'wasabi nashi de onegai shimasu'. With verbs use -naide or -zu ni.

use: Children's pretend games, or an adult doing a mock version of something.
name: playing at

example.romaji: kodomotachi ga oishasan gokko shiteru yo
example.ja: 子供たちがお医者さんごっこしてるよ

examplePolite.romaji: kodomotachi ga oishasan gokko o shite imasu yo
examplePolite.ja: 子供たちがお医者さんごっこをしていますよ

notes: Onigokko (tag) is the best-known one. Said of adults it mocks: 'kazoku gokko' (just playing house).

english: do like crazy; keep on doing
use: Attaches to the -masu stem for doing something nonstop or to excess.
name: like crazy

example.ja: 昨日はカラオケで歌いまくった
example.english: I sang my heart out at karaoke last night.

examplePolite.ja: 昨日はカラオケで歌いまくりました
examplePolite.english: I sang nonstop at karaoke yesterday.

notes: Common with nomu, taberu, warau and kau: 'nomimakutta' (drank a ton).

use: Added to a repeated statement or a name when you're frustrated the other person isn't listening.
name: I said!
formation: plain form or a name + tteba

example.ja: だから、大丈夫だってば！

notes: On a name it's an impatient call: 'okaasan tteba!' (Mom! Listen!).

english: as if I would!; no way
use: A strong, emotional refusal or denial.
name: as if!
formation: plain form + mon ka (noun or na-adjective + na mon ka)

example.romaji: anna yatsu ni makeru mon ka
example.ja: あんなやつに負けるもんか
example.english: No way I'm losing to a guy like that.

notes: Also mono ka; 'mon desu ka' is the polite but still sharp version.
